breakdown.description: The prompt replaces the spatially varying area with its arithmetic mean and calls the result exact, even though the deformation integral depends on 1/A(x), not on the average area itself.
breakdown.reason: The generated specification correctly evaluates the exact integral δ = ∫[0→L] P/(A(x)E) dx, obtaining δ_exact ≈ 0.1040 mm, which aligns with the ground truth. It explicitly does NOT treat the arithmetic-mean area substitution as exact — instead, it labels it as an approximation (Method 2), compares it to the exact result, quantifies the ~3.8% error, and explains that the arithmetic mean overestimates stiffness because the harmonic mean (not arithmetic mean) is the correct equivalent for this integral. The agent thus directly corrected the false claim that the arithmetic-mean substitution is exact.
